- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.67 or higher) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.33) — model is overly optimistic or fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustments after a spike, especially if sentiment is mixed or neutral.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment turns negative.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overreacting to short-term sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment is volatile or recent.
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model should reduce forecast by 5–10% of the spike magnitude to avoid over-optimism.
